primary_endpoint_statement: There is no finite universal C for three arbitrary real dense capped query directions on every finite known graph of treewidth at most two, with symmetric supported matrices, allowed diagonals, operator recovery target, and Frobenius action norm.
status: Analytic proof supplied; subject to the owner's independent review.

theorem.quantifier: For every m>=4 and every X in R^((m+1) x 3) whose rows have Euclidean norm at most one
theorem.inverse_constant: C_2(F_m,X)=sup_{0!=D=D^T supported on F_m} ||D||_2/||DX||_F, with infinity for a noninjective action map
theorem.infimum_over_all_dense_designs: The same lower bound holds after infimizing over all capped X.
theorem.asymptotic_conclusion: The minimax inverse constant diverges as m tends to infinity.

proof_mechanism: A zero apex query row or a dependent triangle gives a supported invisible rank-one matrix.
Projection perpendicular to the apex row gives two-dimensional leaf rows z_i.
An edge-supported rank-one matrix gives C_2 >= 1/min_i ||z_i||.
A tridiagonal path-flow matrix B has BZ equal to an explicitly weighted discrete derivative of c.
Three lowest sine modes contain a nonzero c satisfying the two scalar constraints t^T BZ=0.
The congruence D=L B L^T is supported on the fan, preserves B as a principal block, and makes the apex action vanish.
The slow-flow operator bound and the local small-projection bound combine to give a uniform all-design divergence.
assumptions: The graph and the full fixed query block X may be known when choosing the worst-case D.
The three query directions are real, with a separate Euclidean energy cap one on every row.
Every permitted symmetric coefficient, including every diagonal, is unrestricted in magnitude and sign.
Support means zeros outside the graph edges and diagonal; permitted entries may themselves be zero.
The action error is measured in absolute Frobenius norm, and matrix error is measured in spectral/operator norm.
The impossibility concerns the fixed-block query formulation in the prompt, not a different adaptive or probabilistic success criterion.
decoder_consequence: Even a nonlinear decoder exact on every noiseless supported matrix cannot obey a uniform adversarial Frobenius-action-to-operator-error Lipschitz bound for these three-query designs.
construction_cost: O(m) exact-real arithmetic operations and O(m) sparse storage for the nondegenerate witness after X is supplied and a constant number of trigonometric constants are evaluated; generate the sine modes by recurrence. Bit complexity and numerical conditioning are not asserted.
narrower_results: For any fixed design with minimum apex-orthogonal projected row norm delta>0 and all adjacent projected determinants nonzero, C_2 >= max(1/delta, delta/[2 sqrt(m-1) sin(3 pi/(2m))]).
The fan family alone suffices for the negative endpoint; the argument requires no star-coloring restriction.

Four queries suffice on the fan family by placing the apex on e_4 and cycling leaf rows through e_1,e_2,e_3. The direct decoder has Frobenius and operator error constant at most sqrt(2) and O(m) work/storage. Thus four is the minimum fixed uniformly stable query count for this family.
unresolved: Whether four or five capped real query directions give uniform stability on every treewidth-two graph.
